* * *
 JUDGMENT

Major children of Padma W/o Puttaswamy filed petition under Section 166 of IMV Act claiming compensation from the respondents who are the owner and insurer of Motorcycle bearing No.KA-05-LN-9665 alleging that on 20.11.2022 at 7.30 a.m. when Padma was traveling by sitting on the pillion of motorcycle bearing No.KA-05- LN-9665 on Bengaluru-Mangalore NH-75, in front of Sri Lakshmi Venkateshwara Hotel, near Magadipalya, within the limits of Amruthur police station,
Tumkur District, the rider of the motorcycle rode the same negligently made the motorcycle to fell on the road, thereby caused accident, caused instantaneous death of Padma.
2. As on the date of accident Padma being aged about 59 years, used to earn Rs.20,000/- per month by working as Tailor and used to contribute the entire income to the family.
3. Regarding accident Amruthur police registered a case in crime No.161/2022 against the rider of the motorcycle.
4.
In response to the notice, the respondent No.1- owner of the motorcycle appeared through his advocate, but neither filed written statement nor participated in the proceedings.
5. In response to the notice respondent No.2 insurance company appeared through his Advocate and filed written statement denying the reason and mode of accident, age, occupation and income of Padma.

Respondent No.2-insurance company in para No.5 of the written statement denied the issuance of policy to motorcycle bearing No.KA-05-LN-9665, however in para No.13 of the written statement sought permission to defend the case as insurer of the motorcycle.

6. On the basis of the pleadings on 14.06.2024, this Authority has framed the following issues:
1. Whether the petitioners prove that on 20.11.2022 at about 7.30 a.m. on NH-75,
Bengaluru- Mangalore road, in front of Sri Lakashmi Venkateshwara Hotel, near Magadi Palya, Tumkur District, the death cause to one Padma L., was due to actionable negligence act on the part of the rider of the Motorcycle bearing Reg.

No.KA-05-LN-9665 as alleged?
Venkatesh vs Varalakshmi on 10 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/5202009/
2 2.
Whether the petitioners are entitled to compensation ?
If so, how much and from whom?
3. What order?

7. On 14.06.2024, 10.07.2024, 21.08.2024 petitioner No.3 Raghu deposed as PW1 and produced 13 documents at Ex.P.1 to P.13.
8.
In this case parties does not made arrangements to submit arguments.
I have perused the records.

9. On the basis of the record, my findings on the above issues are as under:
Issue No.1 ...
In the Affirmative, Issue No.2 ...
Petitioners are entitle to receive Rs.11,49,072/- with interest at 6%p..a. from 20.02.2025 as compensation from respondents.
Issue No.3 ...

As per final order for the following:-
REASONS 10. Issue No.1 :- In the evidence PW1 stated that on 20.11.2022 at 7.30 a.m. when Padma was traveling by sitting on the pillion of motorcycle bearing No.KA-05-LN- 9665 on Bengaluru-Mangalore NH-75, in front of Sri Lakshmi Venkateshwara Hotel, near Magadipalya,
within the limits of Amruthur police station, Tumkur District, the rider of the motorcycle rode the same negligently and made the motorcycle to fell on the road, thereby caused accident, caused instantaneous death of Padma.
11.
In the written statement respondent No.2 insurance company denied the allegation regarding reason and mode of accident.
12. In the cross-examination, PW1 stated that he never witnessed the accident.

13. Ex.P.1 is the copy of the FIR pertaining to crime No.161/2022 registered by Amruthur police against Shruti-rider of Motorcycle bearing No.KA-05-LN-9665 for having committed offence punishable under Section 279, 337, 304A of IPC, on the basis of complaint presented by Raghu P.
S/o Late Puttaswamy.
Ex.P.2 is the copy of the complaint.
Ex.P.3 is the copy of the spot mahazar.
Ex.P.4 is the copy of sketch of place of the accident.
Ex.P.7 is the copy of inquest mahazar.
Ex.P.8 is the copy of the PM report.
Ex.P.9 is the motor vehicle accident report.

Ex.P.10 is the copy of the charge sheet filed by Amruthur police in crime No.161/2022 against Shruthi K. W/o Venkatesh P.,
rider of Motorcycle bearing No.KA-05-LN-9665 for having committed the offence punishable under Section 279,337, 304(A) of IPC.
In the police records name of the Padma is noted as pillion rider of Motorcycle bearing No.KA-05-LN- 9665 and victim of the accident.

Venkatesh vs Varalakshmi on 10 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/5202009/
3 14.

In the file there are no evidence to disbelieve the evidence placed by the PW.1 regarding reason,
mode and consequence of the accident.

Hence, I have concluded that on 20.11.2022 at 7.30 a.m.
when Padma was traveling by sitting on the pillion of motorcycle bearing No.KA-05-LN- 9665 on Bengaluru-Mangalore NH-75, in front of Sri Lakshmi Venkateshwara Hotel, near Magadipalya,
within the limits of Amruthur police station, Tumkur District, Shruthi K. W/o Venkatesh P.- rider of the motorcycle rode the same negligently made the motorcycle to fell on the road, thereby caused accident, caused instantaneous death of Padma.
Hence, I answer issue No.1 in the affirmative .

15. Issue No.2: In the evidence PW1 stated that as on the date of accident his mother Padma used to earn Rs.20,000/- per month by working as Tailor and vending flowers and used to contribute entire income to the family.
16. In the written statement respondent No.2 insurance company denied the allegation regarding occupation and income of deceased Padma as on the date of accident.
17. In the cross-examination PW1 stated that his mother used to work as a Tailor in the home and submitted lack of documents regarding occupation and income of his mother.
PW1 denied the suggestion that as on the date of accident his mother neither worked as Taailor nor earned Rs.20,000/- per month.
18. In the inquest mahazar and postmortem report age of deceased is noted as 59 years.
In the copy of the aadhaar card marked at Ex.P.11 date of birth of the deceased Padma is noted as 05.09.1963.

The aadhaar cards shows that petitioners are children of Padma.
19.
In the complaint PW.1 -Raghu stated that his mother was residing with him in Bengaluru.
In the file there are no documents regarding occupation and income of Padma, however mother is always mother.

Hence, I have inferred that it is fit and proper to calculate the loss of dependency presuming that as on the date of accident deceased Padma being aged 59 years 2 months, had notional income as Rs.15,500/- per month, by deducting 1/3rd towards personal expenses and applying multiplier 9 in the following terms:
Approximate age of the deceased as 59 years on the date of accident - 2 months Monthly notional income of deceased - Rs.15,500/- Padma as on the date of accident Less : 1/ 3rd towards personal Rs.10,334/- expenses of the deceased Padma (15,500 - 5,166/- = 10,334) Loss of dependency 10,334 x12x9 Rs.11,16,072/-
20.
Hence, I award Rs.11,16,072/- towards loss of dependency.

Rs.16,500/- towards loss of estate,
Rs.16,500/- towards funeral expenses.
21. There are no documents regarding occupation and income of Padma.
In the complaint PW.1 noted that as on the date of incident Padma his mother residing in his house.
Therefore, while calculating compensation under the head of loss of dependency no amount is added as future prospects.
As the petitioners are the major children of Padma, they are not entitle to receive compensation under the head of consortium.

Hence I came to the conclusion that the petitioners Venkatesh vs Varalakshmi on 10 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/5202009/
4 being the major children of Padma are entitle to receive Rs.11,49,072/- with interest from 20.02.2025 as compensation.

Head of Compensation Amount/

Funeral expenses 16,500-00 Total 11,49,072-00 22.

In the written statement at para No.5 respondent No.2 insurance company denied the issuance of the police to the motorcycle bearing No.KA-05-LN-9665 and in para No.13 of written statement sought permission to defence the case under Sec.170 of MV Act as insurer of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-05-LN-9665.

In the reply marked at Ex.P.6 submitted by the respondent No.1 to the I.O. has noted that as on the date of incident motorcycle had insurance coverage and Shruti-rider of the motorcycle had learner's licence to ride the motorcycle and noted production of insurance documents and DL documents.

The copy of the policy bearing No.3005/2011488631/00/0000035707 available in the file shows that as on the date of incident motorcycle bearing No.KA-05-LN-9665 had insurance coverage with respondent No.2.
Hence, I have inferred that as on the date of incident respondent No.2 is the insurer of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-05-LN-9665, therefore liable to indemnify the respondent No.1.

Hence, I came to the conclusion that respondents being owner and insurer of motorcycle bearing No.KA-05-LN-9665 are liable to pay compensation to the petitioners and an award is to be passed directing the respondents to pay compensation.

Hence, I answer issue No.2 partly in the affirmative and pass the following :
ORDER
The petition filed under Section 166 of IMV Act is hereby partly allowed.

The respondents shall either jointly or severally pay Rs.11,49,072/- (Rupees Eleven lakhs forty nine thousand seventy two only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from 20.02.2025, to petitioners towards compensation.
The respondent No.2, being the insurer of the Motorcycle bearing No.KA-05-LN-9665 shall deposit the compensation amount with interest within 3 months from today.
The compensation amount and interest are distributed among petitioners equally.
After deposit compensation, entire compensation amount and interest may be released to the petitioners by crediting the same to their respective bank accounts directly.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/- .
Draw an Award accordingly.
